analyzed_vuln.description: The cheap-validation overload `ValidateArrayVisitor::Visit(const UnionArray&)` validates union children but never verifies that the union's type-code buffer, and for dense unions its int32 value-offset buffer, are non-null and large enough for `array.offset() + array.length()` elements. Consequently `RecordBatch::ValidateFull()` accepts structurally undersized union buffers, then `ValidateArrayDataVisitor::Visit(const UnionArray&)` iterates to the attacker-declared array length and performs unchecked `type_codes[i]` / `offsets[i]` reads; this PoV reaches the 4-byte out-of-bounds read at validate.cc:380.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A valid IPC stream must describe a record batch containing a dense union column whose metadata-declared row/array length exceeds the number of int32 entries available in its value-offset body buffer (with preceding slots/type codes arranged so validation continues to the missing offset). The IPC reader propagates the declared length and sliced body buffers into `UnionArray`; `RecordBatch::Validate()` calls the deficient cheap union validator and succeeds, after which `ValidateFull()` calls `ValidateArrayData`, whose dense-union offset loop reads beyond the buffer.
